Subject: Emergency Maintenance: KV-cache misrouting — Immediate patch (ETA ~35m)

Hi Emma / Jordan —

We’re seeing a production issue affecting a subset of requests routed to our KV cache layer that can return stale or 5xx responses for particular tokenized keys. This started at ~06:55 PDT and impacts requests with short-lived prefix caching (primarily orgs on multi-tenant pools).

What we’re doing now:
- Pushing an emergency hotfix to correct a routing table regression in the KV cache (Dev team).
- Rolling the patch as a canary across 5% of traffic, then expanding if green.
- Monitoring request success rate, tail latency, and error rate.

Customer impact: transient 500s and increased latency for some requests. No data deletion or cross-tenant leakage has been observed.

ETA & next steps: we expect the initial canary within ~35 minutes and will update at the end of the rollout. We’ll follow with a short postmortem and the patch release notes.

Attachments: hotfix_release_notes_v1.0.pdf (summary), kvcache_patch.diff.tar.gz (patch artifact)

We’ll keep you posted in this thread — please let me know if you need an outage window logged on your end.

Thanks,

Short update / technical note: the issue is in the routing layer that maps token prefixes to shard-local KV instances. A recent optimization changed TTL propagation for ephemeral entries which can cause a key lookup to route to an empty shard briefly — resulting in 404->upstream 500 paths or increased latency while falling back to origin.

Impact scope: read-path only in multi-tenant pools; write-paths and persistent storage are not impacted. Session tokens remain valid. We do not see any auth/session token expiry triggered by this bug.

Planned mitigation: rolling hotfix (patch attached) reverts the TTL propagation change and adds a fast-fail fallback. We’ll push to canary (5%), observe, then 25% -> 100% if metrics are stable. Current ETA to full rollout: ~25 minutes.

Monitoring: I’m watching error-rate by org and will post real-time metrics to the status page.

—Dev

Subject: Postmortem: KV-cache misrouting incident (2026-03-29) — summary & actions

Team / DataLeap / Acme Sec —

Summary (TL;DR):
- Incident window: 2026-03-29 06:55–08:05 PDT (majority resolved by 08:05; verification completed by 09:45).
- Root cause: a regression in a routing optimization changed TTL propagation semantics for ephemeral KV entries; this could route lookups to a shard missing the key and trigger fallback paths that surfaced as 500s.
- Impact: transient increased 5xx rate and tail latency for a subset of multi-tenant pools. No data loss, no auth/session token expiries, no cross-tenant reads detected.

Immediate remediation performed:
- Rolled hotfix v1.0 to revert TTL propagation change and add fast-fail fallback for empty shard responses (rolled canary → 25% → 100%).
- Added metrics and an alert to detect TTL-propagation mismatches.

Follow-up actions (owners & timeline):
- SUP-3456 (Dev): add unit+integration tests for TTL semantics and a canary test harness by 2026-04-05.
- Ops: expand observability on shard-resolution errors, SLA guardrails by 2026-04-02.
- CS (Marissa): run customer outreach for any accounts that saw >1% error increase; status updates complete by 2026-04-01.

Artifacts & links:
- Hotfix notes: hotfix_release_notes_v1.0.pdf (attached)
- Service traces: service_status_log_20260329.csv (attached, redacted)
- Internal ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-3456
- Public status: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-03-29-kvcache
